cards.text: Hosea the prophet is bringing the LORD's words to Israel, and this message opens with an alarm: "Put the ram’s horn to your lips!" An eagle looms over the house of the LORD. Friend, when a message starts with a HORN BLAST, nobody's about to get a compliment.

cards.question: Why does God say the alarm is sounding over His people Israel?

answers.text: They lost a battle at the border

cards.text: Then Israel cries out to God, "O our God, we know You!" That's me telling a baker, "I know this recipe by HEART," while the smoke alarm goes off behind me.

cards.question: After Israel claims to know Him, God answers that Israel has held on to what is good.

cards.text: God says an enemy will pursue Israel. Then He runs down the list of what they've been doing on their own, starting with who's in charge.

cards.question: Israel sets up kings and makes princes. What's God's problem with them?

answers.text: They did it without His approval
They taxed the people too hard

cards.question: Israel takes its own silver and gold and makes ___ for itself, to its own destruction.

cards.text: Then God calls out one idol by name, the calf of Samaria: "My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?" Friend, you don't ask HOW LONG about something that happened once.

cards.question: Where does God say the calf of Samaria came from?

answers.text: It was carried in from Egypt
It was a gift from Assyria

cards.question: God says the calf of Samaria will stand for many years to come.

cards.text: Then comes the big line: "For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind." Read that one twice, friend. I'll wait.

cards.question: God says Israel sows the wind and will reap the whirlwind. What's the picture?

answers.text: What they plant comes back far bigger
Their fields need more rain to grow
A storm will pass right over them

cards.text: Plant a breeze, harvest a TORNADO. And the fields give nothing: what sprouts yields no flour, and even if it did produce, foreigners would swallow it up.
And then: "Israel is swallowed up!" Now they're out among the nations like a worthless vessel. Friend, I KNOW that feeling. Years in the back of a junk drawer under the takeout menus.

cards.question: Israel goes off on its own, like a wild donkey, up to another nation. Which one?
Ephraim hires allies among the nations, and God says those allies will keep Ephraim safe.

cards.text: Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, and they became his altars for sinning. And God says He wrote out the great things of His law for them.

cards.question: God wrote out the great things of His law for Israel, and they regarded it as something ___.

cards.text: Then the sacrifices. They offer them as gifts to God, and they eat the meat. That's me handing a friend a cookie box after I ate every cookie on the drive over. "It's the THOUGHT that counts!"

cards.question: The LORD accepts the sacrifices Israel offers Him as gifts.
God says He will remember Israel's iniquity and punish their sins. Where does He say they will return?

cards.text: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah, the southern kingdom, has multiplied its fortified cities. That's like forgetting your own name but remembering the WiFi password.

cards.question: Israel built palaces and Judah built fortified cities. What does God say He will send upon their cities?
